newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO accuses Israel over land dealer killings.
newsitem.headline: PLO accuses Israel over land dealer killings.

text.p: A PLO security chief said on Wednesday the killing of three Arab land dealers may have been "engineered" by Israel to cover up what he called its failure to honour peace deals signed with the Palestinians.
Amin al-Hindi, director-general of the Palestinian Intelligence Service, offered no evidence to support his allegations that Israel might have had a hand in the killings, which he condemned.

"I believe that all the security issues that happened, and which Israel is trying blame the Palestinian Authority or the security aparatus for, have been engineered to cover up for its failure to honour agreements between the Palestine Liberation Organisation and Israel," Hindi told a news conference.
Michael Stoltz, a spokesman for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, called Hindi's charges "nonsense".
Three Arab land dealers were killed by unknown assailants in the month since the Palestinian Authority announced a ban on the sale of Arab-owned land to Israelis.
The land sales ban was intended to stop Israel from expanding Jewish settlements, the authority said. A Palestinian cabinet member has said breach of the ban would be punishable by death
Israel, blaming the PLO for the killings, on Tuesday sent a letter to the Palestinian Authority demanding an end to the murders.

An Israeli official said on Monday the Jewish state must "consider carefully" before resuming peace talks with the Palestinians, broken off after Netanyahu sent bulldozers to clear land for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Hindi denied his security forces were involved in the killings and said they still had no suspects.
He said the role of his security forces was only to collect information on land dealers and turn it over to the Palestinian Ministry of Justice and the attorney general for legal action.
